claims.statement: Article 50 applies from 2 August 2026 and includes machine-readable marking or disclosure duties for specified AI-generated, manipulated, or interactive content, creating an auditable per-asset workflow event.
Agencies and deployers that publish covered material must allocate production or compliance labor to transparency, but their willingness to license a separate evidence tool is unknown.
A plausible control path is a customer-authorized evidence ledger embedded at final approval, with local-export fallback; no agency data rights or production integration is secured.
The Commission reported more than 180 organizations signed the transparency code before enforcement, indicating active workflow change but not demand for this particular product.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Agency operations, legal/compliance lead, production director, or client account owner
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Vendor neutrality, preservation checks across tool handoffs, and client-ready evidence must be valuable beyond native platform labels
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The agency owns its client relationship; the proposed compliance-tool relationship does not yet exist
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Integration or referral from asset-management, legal, insurance, and agency production partners

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Compliance-partner share, integration partnerships, and targeted agency outreach
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Annual or monthly advance license; integration costs are front-loaded
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Potentially high for metadata-only processing, but creative-tool churn and legal support may be expensive
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Tool-chain mapping, policy configuration, evidence exceptions, and agency onboarding
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Security, GDPR, legal interpretation boundaries, professional liability, and rule updates
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Target 600-3,000 PLN per agency workspace monthly plus volume above included asset records
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Asset inspection compute, hashes and timestamps, storage, signing, notifications, and usage support

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Generative platforms, Adobe-like creative suites, asset-management systems, and publishers can embed compliant marking and logs
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: A sealed compliance evidence record is paid; measurable losses include manual legal review, rework after metadata stripping, and inability to demonstrate the chosen marking or disclosure process
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: First covered AI-content campaign after 2 August 2026, a client assurance request, or a failed platform or legal review
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual license renewal and continued per-asset evidence creation

contrary_evidence: The code is voluntary and firms can demonstrate equivalent compliance by other means.
Large generation and creative platforms are natural owners of provenance features and can bundle them.
Not every AI-assisted marketing asset is covered by the same Article 50 duty.

critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Provide a local command-line or desktop preflight that exports evidence to the agency's own storage without retaining assets
critical_control_point.current_owner: Agencies and clients own their source assets; no venture ledger exists
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The agency owns its client relationship; the proposed compliance-tool relationship does not yet exist
critical_control_point.duration: Unknown until an agency agreement is executed
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Public EU guidance, open metadata standards, and lawful agency outreach are available; no private asset corpus or integration rights are held
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Each agency customer together with its creative and publishing platforms
critical_control_point.renewal: Proposed annual workspace license with customer-controlled evidence retention
critical_control_point.subject: Asset-level provenance, disclosure, and pre-publication evidence dataset

economics.acquisition_route: Compliance advisers, agency operations communities, asset-management integrations, and direct design-partner outreach
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Conditional path: 400 agencies at a 1,500 PLN monthly blended license equals 7.2m PLN ARR; a defensible compliance workflow could exceed 5m PLN in value, but control and willingness to pay are unproven
economics.founder_time: A metadata-only preflight and three design partners fit 3-5 hours daily; deep integrations require later staffing
economics.gross_margin_basis: License revenue less compute, evidence storage, support, integration, channel share, and legal maintenance
economics.payback: Target within one or two avoided manual review cycles per month; unmeasured
economics.pricing: Discovery hypothesis: 600-3,000 PLN per workspace monthly with included volume and metered overage
economics.retention_or_repeat: Recurring with asset volume and annual policies, but vulnerable to platform bundling

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned corpus of tool-chain failure modes and destination-specific marking retention improves preflight rules
fingerprint.customer: EU advertising, social-content, localization, and production agencies using generative AI across multiple tools
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Agency production-tool integrations, compliance advisers, insurer referrals, and white-label client approval portals
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Licensed asset-preflight workflow, machine-readable-mark check, disclosure rules, and immutable evidence export
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The agency pays a workspace license plus metered fees when an asset evidence record is sealed or exported
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A covered AI-assisted asset is approved for client publication after passing through generators, editors, and export tools that may strip metadata

founder_fit: Automated classification, anomaly detection, and evidence lineage fit data-science skills
The work can start as a narrow preflight tool without constant public-facing content creation
Per-asset outcomes and failure modes are measurable
A software-first license can scale beyond Warsaw if platform access proves durable
risks: Overstating legal compliance could create professional liability
Metadata standards and Commission guidance can change
Sensitive unreleased campaign assets create severe security obligations
Platform-native tooling can erase the standalone market

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: agency workspace license plus asset level compliance evidence usage
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: permissioned ledger of asset origin marking checks disclosures and approvals
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: creative and publication tools must expose or preserve enough provenance and metadata for reliable checks

structure.commercial_archetype: Agency workspace license with per-asset evidence events
structure.control_point: The evidence dataset assembled at final creative approval
structure.critical_dependency: Reliable metadata inspection and integration across generation, editing, asset-management, and publication platforms

thesis: Observed compliance-workflow change: EU AI Act Article 50 transparency duties began applying on 2 August 2026, including machine-readable marking and disclosure duties for covered generated or manipulated content, and more than 180 organizations had already signed the related code. License agencies a vendor-neutral preflight and evidence ledger that checks each asset's declared origin, marking, disclosure copy, publication destination, and retained proof before release.
title: AI Content Marking Evidence Ledger for Agencies
uncertainties: Exact agency segments and asset types with repeatable Article 50 exposure
Whether metadata survives real production and publication chains
Legal sufficiency of machine-generated evidence exports
Agency willingness to expose client assets to a new vendor
